name: std::get_deleter

declarations.code:
template <class Deleter, class T>

Deleter *get_deleter(const std::shared_ptr<T> &p) noexcept;

intro: Access to the p's deleter. If the shared pointer p owns a deleter of type cv-unqualified Deleter (e.g. if it was created with one of the constructors that take a deleter as a parameter), then returns a pointer to the deleter. Otherwise, returns a null pointer.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.text:
p

 -

 a shared pointer whose deleter needs to be accessed

sections.title: Return value
sections.text: A pointer to the owned deleter or nullptr. The returned pointer is valid at least as long as there remains at least one shared_ptr instance that owns it.

sections.title: Notes
sections.text: The returned pointer may outlive the last shared_ptr if, for example, std::weak_ptrs remain and the implementation doesn't destroy the deleter until the entire control block is destroyed.
